name: Accessibility equivalence verification
summary: An accessibility option is verified by comparing the objective, actionable meaning, timing, state, and reward path it preserves—not by counting settings or requiring identical presentation.
player_action: The player configures input, text, audio, visual, motion, cognition, or assistance options and performs the same bounded objective.
system_response: The game substitutes channels and interaction forms while declaring any intentional change to information, timing, challenge, scoring, or rewards.
failure_modes: A substitute cue arrives after the response window.
A remapped action remains hard-coded elsewhere.
Text or narration describes stale state.
An assist secretly changes progression, scoring, or encounter identity.
Individually valid options fail when combined.
accessibility: Test with players who use the supported configurations rather than treating guidelines as proof.
Preserve player-owned settings across retry, save migration, platform change, and update.

smallest_playable_test.setup: Run one navigation, combat, puzzle, pickup, journal, death, and save objective under representative remap, hold/toggle, text, contrast, narration, cue-substitution, motion, flash, and assistance combinations.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: Each supported configuration preserves the declared objective and clearly discloses any intentional difference in information, challenge, state, or reward.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: Completion is possible but timing, effort, comfort, or configuration discovery creates avoidable barriers.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: A required objective depends on one sensory or motor channel, settings conflict, or hidden state/reward differences occur.

evidence.claim: Xbox Accessibility Guidelines provide implementation and testing guidance developed with the gaming and disability community for design, development, and test teams.
evidence.notes: Guidelines inform tests but do not replace verification with players.

evidence.claim: EA documents Dead Space menu narration, contrast and color options, remapping, hold/toggle alternatives, aim-assistance controls, and optional content warnings or visual hiding.
evidence.notes: Shows independent configuration across multiple access needs.
